doc.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007

title: Politics: the Bush administration and impeachment
summary: Lellis gives strong opinions on the Bush presidency, the 2000 election and the need for impeachment, and jokes with Rowe about satirical song titles.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Your Bush league. You’re talking about your Bush league. I’m making an educated guess that you’re not too happy with the current state of affairs.

Yeah I think it’s the greatest travesty this country has endured. I thought Nixon was bad, I thought Reagan split up the — in fact I thought Reagan began the entire whole rap movement and all that when he said, I don’t think he was necessarily racist I just think that he said if you don’t have money I’m sorry, I can’t deal with you. And so that took a lot of people and just put them out of society’s flow. And then this guy came along, and he has rewritten all the rules or broken all the rules I think. He is a travesty. I think he is the most detrimental thing this country has endured. Period. I think the election in 2000, I was on the streets the day after the election. I had a sign that said “Supreme C-O-U-R-T” © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

and the bottom said “C-O-U de etat. Because that’s what I think we’ve endured. I think the Supreme Court vote that took one vote to change the national election — you know I just read in the Times that it’s within the Constitution with a majority of Congress they can change the number of Supreme Court justices and it’s been down to five and as high as eleven.

I didn’t know that either. I read it in the Times about three days ago. I was amazed. So that decision and placing this figurehead in office against the popular vote, I just think it’s a travesty. I do everything I can, I write letters, I write funny things, or try to.
Right. My favorite is Condoleeza Rice sings “Oh What a Beautiful Warning.”
You almost have to make some fun.
Well you do. You literally have to make light of it because that’s how devastating it is I feel.
Do you think we can repair it? How? How can we repair it?

I think for the benefit of the country, this man above all, needs to be impeached. I wrote an article that was actually printed — or a letter that was printed in the Long Island, (New York) Newsday and it was about crying wolf. The impeachment of Clinton was a terrible thing. It shouldn’t have happened for an affair between two people. No one other than them. But the result of that was that everyone is now afraid to impeach the actual wolf. Because this guy is the wolf and he’s in the White House. And now everyone’s afraid to go through that process. But constitutionally he’s been abysmal. There are now right wing Heritage Foundation people and left wingers that are now getting together and saying that he needs to be impeached. And there was just a brilliant Bill Moyers Journal two weeks ago that these two opposites were on the air with Bill Moyers saying that for the benefit of this country we need to impeach this man. Because it’s not going to go away. And to leave this precedence is the most detrimental thing to our country that I have witnessed in my lifetime.
Including the late sixties when everything was in such turmoil?

Well at least the late sixties the population rose. They rose up and said enough of this. Enough. Sixty-five thousand deaths. Well we aren’t up to that high but this, you don’t know what this man can do in eighteen months, that’s where we are at this point. And I frankly fear. I fear that under this administration we have crested that hill and we are now © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
on the downward slope as the Roman Empire was. I actually feel that. I’m no expert, this is just my feeling and opinion.
Well and hope for better days is in your song.
